picks.title: Norway suspends electricity grid access for new data centres
picks.rationale: A government decision: Statnett has frozen new data-centre grid connections for a year while Norway drafts a licensing scheme, citing AI power demand. It is the first national moratorium of this kind in Europe.
picks.excerpt: Norway's grid operator Statnett suspended new data centre connection applications for a year. The government says it will use the pause to build a data centre licensing scheme and consider state ownership, amid concern over the AI industry's power demand. Time verified via r.jina.ai.

picks.title: EU countries still can't get it together on AI
picks.axis: policy / EU AI Act national enforcement
picks.rationale: The Commission confirmed that 16 member states have missed the deadline to name national AI Act enforcement authorities. This is a concrete enforcement gap for anyone shipping AI in the EU, reported ahead of the Nov 13 Dublin leaders' meeting.
picks.excerpt: Ahead of the Dublin leaders' meeting on AI (Nov 13), 16 capitals have missed the deadline to appoint a national authority to enforce the AI Act, and Brussels has delayed data centre support because of national administrative holdups. The Commission confirmed the count.

picks.title: Revealed: Palantir lobbied minister to stretch AI tools' reach to NHS GP records
picks.axis: policy / AI procurement and health data privacy (UK)
picks.rationale: Original documentary reporting from ministerial WhatsApp messages on how an AI vendor sought access to GP records through a public procurement platform. Attribute the account to the Guardian's reporting.
picks.excerpt: WhatsApp messages seen by the Guardian show Palantir pressing health minister Zubir Ahmed to help bring sensitive GP record data into its NHS AI platform.

picks.title: AI 안경 쓰고 시험 치다 적발된 중·고생 4명…전원 0점 처리
picks.axis: policy / government enforcement on AI devices (Korea)
picks.rationale: A follow-up with a new official outcome: the Ministry of Education's nationwide survey found 4 smart-glasses cheating cases in school exams, and every student involved received a zero. The orchestrator assigned this story to politics.
picks.excerpt: 교육부는 전국 중·고교를 대상으로 스마트 안경 내신평가 부정행위를 전수조사해 4건(중1·고3)을 확인했다. 적발된 학생은 모두 0점 처리됐다.

picks.title: Deepfake Penalties Rejected 20–15
picks.rationale: A concrete legislative vote, which covers the deepfake/elections axis: Bahrain's Shura Council rejected 20–15 a bill that would have criminalised deepfake misuse. The outlet is off-list, but none of the listed outlets carried the vote.
picks.excerpt: Bahrain's Shura Council voted 20–15 to reject a bill with criminal penalties for deepfake misuse, amid debate sparked by a fake video of a Shura member.

dedup.note: Dropped: EU presses OpenAI/Anthropic on safety incidents (Rapporteur). It carries a history_match to the 10-15 Euronews 'first enforcement test over lab incidents' and is the same running GPAI-incident enforcement story with no clearly distinct formal decision, so it is treated as a duplicate. Nvidia/Huang affair (Ars) is a follow-up to 11-07; the new element is a corporate board probe, not a government decision, ruling or filing, so it was dropped. The Verge COP31 pledge piece is opinion about an intergovernmental pledge, and the Freedom House podcast (Tech Policy Press) and the CSET preview are commentary/analysis; all three were dropped. Deprioritised on score/diversity: Trump 60 Minutes (an interview statement, not a document), Google schools Search policy (weaker politics axis), PM-Macron readout (generic), the Rest of World talent feature, the etnews AI education budget cut (it would be a second etnews card and is at the budget-proposal stage), Yonhap defense AI institutes and ITU, and the Tulfo bill. Cross-section: the smart-glasses story is assigned to politics by the orchestrator. published_urls.json (4192 lines) is too large to read in full with Read-only tools, so the exact-grep across sections was not done. None of the five URLs is a politics URL in history_digest. The Palantir/NHS item should be grep-checked against medicine before roll.
